text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- The Housing Fund said it would give favourable housing loans of a total of three billion tolars ($19 million) to families that have at least three children.
- June monthly inflation rose 0.4 percent, down from 1.3 percent in May, the Statistical Office said.
- Privatisation vouchers, which were given to all citizens at the end of 1993, expired on the last day of June.

- Marjan Podobnik, president of the conservative People's Party, which is a coalition partner of leading centre-left Liberal Democrats, said legislation that would protect national interests after Slovenia becomes an association member of the European Union was the party's priority.
- Slovenia and Austria ended renovation of border tunnel Ljubelj in the Alps on Monday where part of the ceiling collapsed last year, hurting three people.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will visit Slovenia after the NATO summit in Madrid, which will take place on July 8 and 9.
- The Chamber of Commerce said the government should make cutting public spending a priority in order to improve competitiveness of the country's economy.
- Economic ministers of the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) states will meet in Slovenia's tourist resort of Bled on Thursday and Friday.
- Duty-free shops on the Slovenian border with Austria expect a fall in sales of cigarettes due to Austria's decision to limit the allowed duty-free import to only 25 cigarettes.
